sources: SUNDAY Oct 4 2026 RUN (06:13 UTC, weekend - all market fields are Friday Oct 2 closes or Oct 1-2 official prints). HEADLINE: CREDIT MADE IT NINE STRAIGHT SESSIONS - HY OAS 324BP - AND THE G7 BROKE THE OIL RALLY. CREDIT - NINE CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS, AND THIS IS THE NEW INFORMATION IN TODAY'S RUN: ICE BofA US High Yield OAS 324bp (FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2, 3.24 pct dated Oct 1), a NINTH consecutive session of widening and the largest single-day move of the run at plus 12bp. Yesterday's run carried 312bp dated Sep 30; the Oct 1 print has since landed and it accelerated. Full sequence: 268 (Sep 18), 266 (Sep 21), 268 (Sep 22), 273 (Sep 23), 280 (Sep 24), 293 (Sep 25), 302 (Sep 28), 308 (Sep 29), 312 (Sep 30), 324 (Oct 1) - 56bp of widening with not one day of retracement. For nine runs this has been the cleanest stress signal on the dashboard, it widened BEFORE the labour data arrived, and it is now widening FASTER after it. Note the print is dated Oct 1, so it does NOT yet contain the Friday payroll reaction - the Monday print matters. OIL - THE G7 CAPPED THE SHOCK: Brent 102.25 USD/Bbl (Friday Oct 2 settle, EnergyNow and TradingEconomics), DOWN 0.06 pct on the day and just plus 0.11 pct on the week after adjusting for contract rollover - effectively FLAT, versus the 'up' trend carried in the last three runs. The reversal driver is policy, not geology: the G7 agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of emergency oil and diesel reserves over several months after US pressure and Trump's export-ban threat (Washington Post Oct 2, The National Oct 2, Time Oct 3). That knocked WTI to 91.11 (minus 1.90 pct on the day, minus 1.41 pct on the week) while Brent held above 102, because the release targets refined products - tight diesel - rather than crude scarcity. Thursday's rally on China's fuel-export suspension and the third US carrier was reversed within a session. Intraday Friday headlines had Brent as low as near 99 before it recovered. The war premium is now being actively fought by coordinated government intervention; trend downgraded from up to flat. LABOUR - FRIDAY'S CRACK STILL THE BACKDROP: September nonfarm payrolls plus 29,000 against plus 90,000 consensus, unemployment 4.2 pct, August revised down to plus 133,000 (BLS Employment Situation, Oct 2). SAHM RULE 0.00 for September (FRED SAHMREALTIME, released Oct 2), UP from minus 0.07 in August and the first non-negative print of this cycle; the trigger is plus 0.50 so this is not a recession signal, but it is the first time the three-month average unemployment rate has stopped falling relative to its twelve-month low. Direction, not level. Next print Nov 6. FED - THE HIKE IS GONE: bond traders now price a 16 pct chance of a hike, versus 64 pct one week ago (Yahoo Finance, Oct 2 close). The Oct 3 run had this at about 20 pct, the Oct 1 run at 38 pct. Eleven runs of a hiking path priced out in two sessions. RATES: 2s10s 0.45 (FRED T10Y2Y, Oct 2 - a FRESH print versus the Oct 1 value carried yesterday), down 1bp from 0.46 on Oct 1 but up from 0.41 (Sep 30), 0.37 (Sep 29) and 0.32 (Sep 28) - the curve absorbed the payroll report with almost no net change, which is notable given how violently Fed odds moved. Still the steepest of the episode. 10y 5.28 pct (Yahoo Finance, Oct 2 close, plus 0.76 pct on the day), which resolves yesterday's unresolved 5.18-versus-5.28 question in favour of 5.28 - the long end did NOT rally on the weak jobs print. That is the stagflation tell. BREAKEVENS STILL ANCHORED: 5y5y forward 2.35 pct (FRED T5YIFR, Oct 2, fresh print), down 1bp from 2.36 on Oct 1 and versus 2.35 on Sep 28. Brent has round-tripped 30 dollars down, 6 dollars up and back to flat, the labour market cracked, and long-run inflation expectations have moved 1bp. Tested in both directions three times now; has not broken. EQUITY VOL - THE DIVERGENCE WITH CREDIT WIDENS: VIX 15.31 (Cboe, Oct 2 close), down 6.59 pct on the day as equities RALLIED on the weak payroll print (S&P 500 7,722.72 plus 0.73 pct, Nasdaq 27,190.86 plus 1.19 pct). But versus 14.87 on Sep 25 the VIX is UP about 3 pct on the week, so the one-week trend is up even though the daily move was down - trend revised from down to up on the weekly basis. Bad news is good news for equities because it kills the hike. Second consecutive run in which equity vol and credit spreads point in opposite directions, and credit is now moving faster. BOND VOL: MOVE 105.74, carried from the Friday Oct 2 TradingView TVC-MOVE close verified in the Oct 3 run - markets have been shut since, so the level is current, but DATA FLAG: no free MOVE source was independently reachable this run (investing.com quote stale at Feb 10, MacroMicro 403, TradingView scrape returned an implausible 83.99, CNBC 403). Still roughly plus 14 pct over one week and off the 106.61 record of Oct 1. Trend up. FINANCIAL CONDITIONS STILL ASLEEP: NFCI minus 0.548 for the week ending Sep 25 (FRED NFCI), no new release at run time - sequence minus 0.560 (Sep 4), minus 0.558 (Sep 11), minus 0.553 (Sep 18), minus 0.548 (Sep 25). Half a basis point of index tightening over three weeks against 56bp of HY widening and a record MOVE. Conditions remain at the loosest of the cycle. Carried as flat. The divergence is now six weeks old and is the single biggest unresolved question here. DOLLAR: DXY 101.93 (TradingEconomics, Oct 2), down 0.16 pct on the day as the weak employment data ended a four-session advance, but UP 0.9 pct on the week - a third consecutive weekly gain - and plus 3.06 pct on the month. Trend up. COPPER/GOLD 1.57, unchanged. Copper 6.49 USD/Lbs, on track for a nearly 3 pct WEEKLY decline on weakening Chinese industrial activity; gold 4,140.19 USD/t.oz, a second consecutive weekly decline and minus 7.45 pct on the month (both TradingEconomics Oct 2). 6.49/4140.19*1000 = 1.57. Both legs falling together, so the ratio is uninformative this week - it is not signalling a growth impulse. Flat. Global liquidity 1 (stable). REAL ECONOMY - SOFT AND DECELERATING: ISM manufacturing 54.5 for September (ISM, released Oct 1), down from 54.6 in August, with prices paid at 77.9 - still expansionary but decelerating with cost pressure building, the stagflationary mix. Trend down. Initial claims 197k for the week ending Sep 26 (FRED ICSA, no new print - next release Oct 8), down 1k from 198k and still historically low; this remains the ONE indicator that has not confirmed the payroll weakness and it is the key number this Thursday. Flat. UMich consumer sentiment 48.1 (final September, revised UP from the 47.3 preliminary, minus 3.6 points from 51.7 in August, a four-month low, one-year inflation expectations 4.6 pct); next print Oct 9. Building permits 1,403k (August; 1,433k July, 1,374k June), next release Oct 20. LEI 99.5 for August with six-month growth of minus 0.1 pct; y/y carried at about minus 0.7 pct, next release mid-October. CARRIED STANDING ASSUMPTIONS, no free live source: SOFR-OIS 0bp, EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis minus 10bp. BDTI DATA FLAG - THIRTEENTH consecutive run carried at 4,899 and formally non-informative. Investing.com remains frozen at 1,107 dated 31/03, Barchart and MacroMicro inaccessible, Baltic Exchange subscription-only. Public commentary puts the real BDTI all-time high near 1,900 points, so 4,899 is not on a comparable scale and must NOT be read as a level. Wire a paid source or drop the tile. PICTURE: yesterday's run was about the labour market cracking. Today's run is about credit refusing to stop, and about policy stepping in to cap the oil shock. HY OAS went to 324bp on Oct 1 - the ninth straight widening session and the biggest daily move of the sequence - and that print predates the payroll report entirely. Meanwhile the G7's 100 million barrel release broke the two-day crude rally: WTI fell 1.9 pct, Brent held 102 but is now flat on the week, and the energy impulse that threatened to collide with a weakening labour market has been administratively capped, at least for now. The awkward combination is that the 10y did NOT rally on a plus 29k payroll print - it rose to 5.28 pct - while the hike was being priced out, equities rallied and the VIX fell. Long rates refusing to fall on bad growth news, credit widening nine sessions straight, record bond vol, and the broadest measure of financial conditions registering none of it. Either the NFCI is the wrong instrument for this episode or credit and the long end are wrong, and six weeks in that question has not moved closer to an answer. WATCH: whether HY OAS makes it ten sessions on the Monday print and whether the payroll reaction widens it further; whether initial claims on Oct 8 finally confirm the payroll weakness or keep contradicting it at 197k; whether the NFCI release this week turns up after six weeks of divergence; whether the 10y holds 5.28 or finally breaks lower; whether MOVE holds above 100; whether the G7 release caps Brent below 105 or the war premium rebuilds through it; and ISM services plus CPI as the next tests of the prices-paid impulse.
